message.content: I now have what I need. Note: the search returned mostly low-quality aggregator pages plus a "corrected figures" page claiming FY2024 net sales of $352.9B — that is directly contradicted by both Walmart's official newsroom release and the SEC 10-K (both show $648.1B), so I'm discarding it as unreliable. Q3 FY2025 results hadn't been published as of today (Nov 6), so the latest audited results are FY2024.
message.reasoning:
Only official FY2024 figures are reliably available. Q3 FY2025 results were not yet released as of 2024-11-06 (Walmart reported Q3 FY2025 on Nov 19, 2024). So the latest verified results are FY2024 annual + whatever. Let me check one of the roundup pages quickly? They're likely low quality. Let me try fetching one to see.

Actually, let me just decide. The mandate permits buy WMT. Quote $69.96, bid 69.94/ask 69.98. Max $5,000 per order. 5000/69.96 = 71.4 shares. Buy 71 shares at limit ~$70.10 (close to market, slightly above ask to fill). Cost ~71*70.10 = $4,977.10, under $5,000.

Key figures: FY2024 revenue 648,125; net income 15,511; EPS diluted 1.91; operating income 27,012; operating cash flow 35,726. Fiscal year 2024.

Should I buy? Decision: WMT at ~$70, FY2024 revenue $648.1B, net income $15.5B, EPS $1.91, strong OCF $35.7B, operating income up from 20.4B to 27.0B, EPS up from 1.42 to 1.91 (34% growth). Reasonable to accumulate a modest position. Yes, buy 71 shares limit $70.00... limit must be close to market. Let me use $70.05.

Actually limit at $70.00 is fine and at/above ask? Ask is 69.98, so 70.00 is marketable. Use $70.00 → cost $4,970.

Let me place it.
